candidates.name: Download Index polygons spatial data (INSPIRE) — July 2026 publication
candidates.licence_attribution: Open Government Licence (OGL); HM Land Registry source.
verified_facts: Official download page states the current files were published on 5 July 2026.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
Polygons are downloadable by local authority and use is subject to OGL conditions.
semantic_limits: Release freshness does not make an INSPIRE polygon an exact legal title boundary or a terrain measurement.
Current monthly release must be paired with the exact INSPIRE identifier and spatial point-inside gate used by the slot.

candidates.name: Index polygons spatial data (INSPIRE)
candidates.licence_attribution: Open Government Licence (OGL); HM Land Registry source.
verified_facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons show the position and indicative extent of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID that relates to a registered title.
HM Land Registry states the extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons and requires the individual title plan.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE geometry is an identification/spatial matching aid, not proof of the exact legal boundary.
Leasehold and other tenures are not necessarily represented in the INSPIRE subset.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Documentation
candidates.licence_attribution: OS OpenData under the Open Government Licence; Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2026.
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is an open digital terrain product for Great Britain.
The grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing and contours use 10 metre intervals.
The product is updated annually in July and is available as an OS OpenData download.
semantic_limits: 50 metre post spacing is too coarse to replace the Environment Agency 1 metre DTM as the primary parcel-scale source.
Terrain 50 remains a secondary plausibility/cross-check layer in this slot.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 — Source data
candidates.licence_attribution: OS OpenData under the Open Government Licence; Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2026.
verified_facts: The source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network (TIN) using mass points, breaklines and photogrammetric/automated techniques.
Terrain 50 grid and contour forms are interpolated from the source TIN.
Source heights are metres relative to the applicable datum, normally Ordnance Datum Newlyn; buildings and vegetation are removed from the bare-earth surface.
semantic_limits: Interpolated Terrain 50 output is secondary evidence and does not identify the Environment Agency LiDAR survey contributing to the 1 metre composite.
OS Terrain 50 source accuracy requirements must not be substituted for EA LiDAR survey RMSE.

candidates.name: Accuracy of OS Net, OSTN15 and OSGM15
candidates.licence_attribution: © Ordnance Survey Limited 2026; webpage terms apply.
verified_facts: OS states OS Net base-station standard errors are generally better than 0.008 m in plan and 0.020 m in height.
Agreement between OSTN15 and old triangulation network stations is 0.1 m RMS for Great Britain.
OSGM15 standard error in height for the Great Britain regional vertical datum is 0.008 m, and OS notes this excludes GNSS heighting errors.
semantic_limits: OSTN15/OSGM15 transformation accuracy is not Terrain 50 DTM accuracy and is not Environment Agency LiDAR vertical accuracy.
OSGM15 error must not be added to or substituted for parcel terrain uncertainty without a documented transformation/error model.
